study.title: Blessed are all who fear the LORD
study.intro: Psalm 128 is a family blessing. It pictures the ordinary good life of someone who honors God: enjoying the fruit of honest work, a flourishing marriage, children gathered around the table. Then the blessing widens to the whole city and nation, and to grandchildren yet to come. Coming right after Psalm 127, it shows what a house built by the LORD looks like.
study.context: This Song of Ascents may have been spoken as a blessing over pilgrims or families at the temple. In an agricultural society, eating what you grew without losing it to enemies or famine was a sign of God's favor (Deuteronomy 28). Vines and olive trees were Israel's most valued plants. The psalm ends with 'Peace be upon Israel!', as Psalm 125 does.
study.peopleNote: No author is named. The psalm describes a man who fears the LORD, his wife, children and grandchildren as a picture of blessing, not a rule that blessing only comes this way. God is never portrayed as a human figure in planned art.

verses.title: Fear and walk
verses.heading: Who walk in His ways
verses.meaning: 'Blessed are all who fear the LORD, who walk in His ways!' The blessing is open to 'all' who fear the LORD. To fear Him means to honor Him with awe and trust. And that inner reverence shows up in how you walk, the daily path of choices you make. Blessing is not a reward earned by perfect performance; it is the natural fruit of a life oriented toward God.
verses.context: Proverbs 1:7 says the fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge. Psalm 1:1-3 also begins with 'blessed' and describes a life rooted in God's word. Deuteronomy 10:12 asks Israel to fear the LORD and walk in all His ways.
explore: Fear the LORD
Deep reverence and awe toward God that leads to trust and obedience, not terror.
Walk in His ways
Live day by day following God's instructions and character.
verses.reflect: What does it look like for you to walk in God's ways this week, in ordinary choices?
verses.alt: A man walking a path between fields at early morning.

verses.title: Eating the fruit of your labor
verses.heading: Blessings and prosperity will be yours
verses.meaning: 'For when you eat the fruit of your labor, blessings and prosperity will be yours.' In the ancient world, people often worked hard only to lose their harvest to enemies, drought or oppressive rulers. Being able to enjoy what you worked for was a real blessing. God cares about ordinary work and ordinary meals. Honest labor and the simple enjoyment of its fruit are gifts from His hand.
verses.context: Deuteronomy 28:33 warns of strangers eating the fruit of your land as a curse. Ecclesiastes 3:13 says that to eat, drink and find satisfaction in work is the gift of God. Isaiah 65:22 promises God's people will long enjoy the work of their hands.
explore: Fruit of your labor
What your work produces, like a harvest from the fields you planted.
Prosperity
Well-being and things going well, the Hebrew word for good.
verses.reflect: How can you thank God today for the ordinary fruit of your work?
verses.alt: A family sharing bread and fruit at a simple outdoor table.

verses.title: Vine and olive shoots
verses.heading: Sons like olive shoots
verses.meaning: 'Your wife will be like a fruitful vine flourishing within your house, your sons like olive shoots sitting around your table.' The home is pictured like a garden. A vine gives grapes and shade, a picture of a wife's life and fruitfulness. Young olive shoots grow up around an old tree and will one day bear fruit for generations. The family table becomes a place of growth, life and joy.
verses.context: Vines and olive trees were Israel's most valued crops. Olive trees can live for centuries, and new shoots sprout from their roots. Proverbs 31:10-31 praises a capable wife whose children rise up and bless her.
explore: Vine
A grapevine, valued for fruit, wine and shade; a frequent biblical picture of fruitfulness.
Olive shoots
Young sprouts growing up around the base of an olive tree, future fruit-bearing trees.
verses.reflect: What would make your table, wherever and with whomever you eat, a place where people grow?
verses.alt: A grapevine climbing a courtyard wall above a family table.

verses.title: This is the blessing
verses.heading: Blessing shall come to the man who fears
verses.meaning: 'In this way indeed shall blessing come to the man who fears the LORD.' The psalm pauses to underline its point. These ordinary goods, work, food, family, are how God's blessing often shows up. Not every faithful person has all of them, and Scripture knows that well, but they remain good gifts. The emphasis is on the source: blessing flows from fearing God, not from chasing blessings themselves.
verses.context: Jesus said to seek first the kingdom of God and these things will be added (Matthew 6:33). 1 Timothy 4:8 says godliness has value for the present life and the life to come. James 1:17 says every good gift comes from above.
explore: Indeed
Truly, certainly; used to underline that a statement is reliable.
Blessing
God's favor bringing well-being, life and flourishing.
verses.reflect: Are you seeking God's blessings or seeking God Himself? What is the difference in your life?
verses.alt: Late afternoon sun over a small farm with terraced fields.

verses.title: Blessing from Zion
verses.heading: See the prosperity of Jerusalem
verses.meaning: 'May the LORD bless you from Zion, that you may see the prosperity of Jerusalem all the days of your life,' Now the blessing is spoken over the listener. God's blessing comes 'from Zion,' from His dwelling among His people. And the blessing is not just private; it is to see the whole community flourish. A faithful family belongs to a faithful people, and our well-being is tied up with the good of God's city.
verses.context: Numbers 6:24-26 gives the priestly blessing spoken over Israel. Psalm 134:3 also says, 'May the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth, bless you from Zion.' Jeremiah 29:7 links the welfare of the city with the welfare of its people.
explore: From Zion
From God's dwelling place in Jerusalem, the temple where His presence was known.
All the days of your life
For the whole length of a person's life, without interruption.
verses.reflect: How is your own well-being connected to the well-being of your church and community?
verses.alt: A priest's raised hands silhouetted at a temple gate over arriving families.

verses.title: Children's children
verses.heading: Peace be upon Israel!
verses.meaning: 'that you may see your children’s children. Peace be upon Israel!' The blessing stretches across generations. To live long enough to hold your grandchildren was a sign of a full life. Faith that is passed down becomes a legacy. And the psalm ends with peace for all of God's people. One faithful household becomes part of a much bigger story of God's peace across the generations.
verses.context: Proverbs 17:6 says grandchildren are the crown of the aged. 2 Timothy 1:5 mentions Timothy's sincere faith that lived first in his grandmother Lois and mother Eunice. Psalm 103:17 says God's loving devotion extends to children's children.
explore: Children's children
Grandchildren, a picture of long life and a family continuing.
Legacy
What is passed on to the next generations, including faith, values and stories.
verses.reflect: What kind of faith legacy do you hope to pass on to the generations after you?
verses.alt: An older couple seated under an olive tree with grandchildren around them.
